ctx.x: I always had two banjos. You know what I mean? I've been having that for about four years. But what kind of... Well, you say he borrowed one once and went to Jackson, huh?
Went to Jackson, yeah. And never did give it back to him. Never did.
Well, did he hock them or what? I don't know what he'd done to him. No, he didn't hock them.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1959-09-24
items.q: You know this fellow, Ida? Willie Jackson? ... He was singing at Tom Anderson's, right at Iberville and Ramport.

ctx.x: Or Albert Burbank. Albert Burbank, yeah.

Well when he was, you know, didn't have a regular job, but whenever I wanted a client to play and couldn't get Pico, I'd get him. And then sometime I'd get this fellow, George, George Thomas, that's cornbread. Oh yeah, yeah. Brother Conrad. Brother Conrad, yeah. I'd get him. I'd get him to play and he'd play when we'd have a job or so. You know this fellow, Ida? Willie Jackson?
No, I never, a singer? Singer, yeah. New Orleans, they call it New Orleans Willie Jackson. Yeah, Willie Jackson.
